assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened a tunable platform for flat-band, correlated-insulator and superconducting physics. The discovery is original (a theoretical flat-band prediction followed by an experimental demonstration) and has created a field of moire materials. As an experimentalist in materials and imaging I value that the result rests on carefully fabricated, characterized structures and has been explored with many probes, including electron and scanning-probe microscopy.
assessment.attribution: The decisive pair is the Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum-model prediction of flat bands at the magic angle and the Jarillo-Herrero group's 2018 observation of correlated insulation and superconductivity. Rafi Bistritzer and MacDonald share the theory credit; I propose MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero as a two-person configuration, noting that this leaves out Bistritzer and that the supplied list does not include other contributors to the earliest experimental work.
assessment.maturity: Independently reproduced in many laboratories, with a large body of follow-on work (twisted multilayers, TMDs, fractional states). The origin of the superconductivity is still debated, but the discovery itself, flat bands with correlated phases at the magic angle, is robust, and recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism in the superconducting phase remains unsettled.
Whether the prize should reward the theory and experiment together or wait for more settled applications is a judgement call.
Allocation between Bistritzer and MacDonald is unresolved; I have not verified the detailed history of the experimental credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks use a magic-wavelength lattice to trap many atoms and reach fractional uncertainties around 1e-18, a decisive advance in measurement precision with consequences for time standards, relativistic geodesy and tests of fundamental physics. The idea is clear and the invention is concrete, which fits the 'discovery or invention' criterion.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and demonstrated early strontium lattice clocks; Ye's group drove the record precision and many-body clock work. The two-name list is clean and supports a fair configuration, although the list omits other contributors (for example in the broader field of optical clocks), which I cannot assess from the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Mature: multiple independent clocks at the 1e-18 level, international comparisons and ongoing work toward redefinition of the second. Recognition would be timely.
uncertainties: Whether the prize is better directed to a broader optical-clock group (including ion clocks) is unresolved.
Redefinition of the second has not yet happened, which could mean the application impact is still developing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: ARPES gave direct momentum-resolved measurements of electronic structure and became the key spectroscopic tool for high-temperature superconductors, topological materials and correlated systems. This is a methods-driven contribution with broad impact, the type of instrument and technique advance I regard highly because the quality of the measurement determines what physics can be learned.
assessment.attribution: Credit is spread across several groups. Shen, Campuzano and Johnson are credited for the application of ARPES to cuprates and quantum materials; the underlying technique has a longer history (photoemission physics, and instrumentation such as the Scienta analyzers) not captured in the three names, which makes a clean attribution to these three uncertain.
assessment.maturity: Well-established and used worldwide for decades; the interpretation of cuprate spectra is still not complete, but the technique and its key findings (Fermi surface, gap symmetry, kinks) are independently confirmed.
uncertainties: Method versus discovery: the prize is for a specific discovery or invention, and the original instrumentation credit is diffuse.
Several important contributors are not in the credited list; I cannot verify all of that history.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reproducible large room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance in magnetic tunnel junctions made spintronic read heads and magnetic random-access memory practical. The physics (spin-dependent tunneling in thin-film oxide barriers) and the technology impact are both substantial, and the materials-science and interface-quality aspects are central, close to my own area of interfaces and oxides.
assessment.attribution: Miyazaki and Moodera independently reported room-temperature TMR in 1995; Parkin's work on MgO-based junctions and technological development extended it. The three-person configuration is plausible, but there are overlapping contributions (for example from the coherent-tunneling MgO theory and experiments by other groups) that the supplied credit does not include, and the relative role of Parkin versus Miyazaki and Moodera deserves care.
assessment.maturity: Mature: the effect is used in commercial devices for decades and has been independently reproduced. The related GMR prize in 2007 lowers novelty somewhat but the discovery is distinct.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2007 GMR prize may be seen as incremental by some members.
MgO coherent tunneling contributors are not in the supplied credit and the split with Parkin's contribution is unclear.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Neodymium-iron-boron magnets are the strongest permanent magnets and underpin motors, generators, hard drives and energy technologies. This is a clear invention with enormous practical impact and a direct link to materials physics and microstructure control, including the role of grain-boundary phases, which are an electron-microscopy topic.
assessment.attribution: Sagawa (Sumitomo) and Croat (General Motors) discovered the compound independently in 1983-84 by different routes (sintered and melt-spun). The two-name credit is plausible and bounded, but the independent parallel discovery and the corporate setting could make allocation sensitive, and I cannot fully verify the details.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature, with four decades of use and no doubt about the result; the prize would be late rather than premature. A question is whether it is considered physics enough for the physics prize, given that the discovery is materials engineering.
uncertainties: Whether the discovery is judged physics rather than materials engineering or chemistry.
Priority and allocation between Sagawa and Croat, and the roles of others, is only partly clear to me.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical detection and coherent control of single nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond opened a room-temperature solid-state quantum platform with applications in nanoscale magnetometry, thermometry and bioimaging. As someone who works with nanoscale imaging, I see the sensing capability as having broad real impact on materials and life science.
assessment.attribution: Wrachtrup and Jelezko first showed optical detection of single NV spins and coherent control; Lukin contributed to quantum registers and sensing protocols, along with others like Awschalom, Hanson and Yacoby who are not in the list. A fair three-person configuration is not obvious.
assessment.maturity: Substantially confirmed by many groups, and the technology is moving into applications, though some of the sensing impact is still developing; recognition would be fairly timely.
uncertainties: Other major contributors (not in the credited list) may be needed for a fair allocation.
Mixed discovery: single-spin detection, quantum registers and sensing may deserve different recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cirac and Zoller's 1995 proposal for quantum gates with trapped ions and their later theory of quantum simulation with cold atoms laid the conceptual basis for two experimental fields. The originality and clarity are very high.
assessment.attribution: The two-person credit is clean and well matched to the specific theoretical contribution; the experimental realization (Wineland, Blatt and others) is separate and partly already recognized in 2012. The overlap with B016 on cold-atom simulation would need to be handled.
assessment.maturity: Mature in the sense that trapped-ion quantum computing and simulation are well established, and the proposal is widely recognized. As a theory prize it depends on experimental proof, which exists.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 Nobel Prize (Wineland, Haroche) and with the Hubbard-model candidate B016.
Whether a theory-focused prize is preferable to one awarded for experimental realization.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum anomalous Hall effect gives quantized edge transport without an external magnetic field, observed in magnetically doped topological-insulator thin films grown by molecular beam epitaxy. It is a materials-driven discovery, dependent on high-quality epitaxy and characterization, with a clear measurable signature.
assessment.attribution: Fang and Dai co-authored the theoretical prediction for Cr/Fe-doped Bi2Se3-family materials, and Xue led the experimental observation in 2013. This provides a natural theory-plus-experiment configuration, but the relation to the Haldane model and to other theoretical proposals and independent experimental confirmations (for example Chang, Moodera, Wang) is complicated by credit not in the supplied list.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed by other groups, but the quantization temperature is low and applications are still developing. A prize may be somewhat early, and the topological-insulator candidates may be considered together.
uncertainties: Relationship to the topological insulator candidates and the 2016 prize on topological phases.
Credit for the first experimental observation involves other groups that are not on the supplied list.
